determination.question: research why our A/R over 90 has been climbing and what it will take to bring it down
determination.statement: Every figure in this study is measured on your own data. The background notes shaped which readings were taken and never what any number says. A/R over 90 days is inventory that never got billed or never got worked, not payers holding money longer: $10,530,563 of open inventory on a running filing clock has already passed its filing deadline and another $7,301,362 sits with more than 90 days of runway left (F6), while average days to pay in August 2025 ran from 5.5 days at Atlas Commercial to 10.8 days at Veritas Comp Fund (F12), and bill lag held flat through the settled months at roughly 13 days institutional and 6 days professional (F9). Bringing it down takes two moves — submitting the unbilled backlog that is still inside its filing window, $2,427,549 at 61 to 90 days of runway plus the $7,301,362 beyond 90 days (F6), and working the denial queue, where between 62.7% at Summit Peak Medicare Advantage and 74.5% at State Medicaid MCO of denials sit untouched across 5,113 records (F5). Concentration is not where the fix lies, because the over-90 share is house-wide: every payer reads between 37.1% at State Medicaid and 51.6% at Atlas Commercial (F1), and every facility between 41.5% at Eastmere Medical Center and 47.3% at Central Physicians Plaza (F8). The aging is also almost entirely deep rather than ordinary payer float — $14,105,052 sits in the 120-plus bucket against $1,029,313 in 91 to 120 (F3), and the over-120 share tracks the over-90 share closely at each payer (F2). Denials are not what fills that tail: only $107,003 of denied dollars sit in the 120-plus bucket, against $972,607 at 31 to 60 days (F4). Aiming the work, the 120-plus balance concentrates at Atlas Commercial with $3,076,604 and State Medicaid with $2,389,661 (F13), and by service line at Orthopedic Surgery with $3,891,681 (F14), with $8,262,517 of that bucket professional against $5,842,535 institutional (F11). The same two names carry the unbilled exposure — Atlas Commercial holds $2,422,818 of the past-deadline inventory (F7), of which Orthopedic Surgery is $1,337,996 (F10). Within Orthopedic Surgery the split matters: $2,874,481 is already expired, but $1,881,233 still has more than 90 days of runway and $723,787 has 61 to 90 (F15), so a single billing queue can still reach a large share of it. Recoverability of the $10,530,563 past its filing deadline was also not measured (F6), so that block should be treated as a separate write-off question from the queues above. 1 reading here measures a rate over a counted population, across 5,113 records behind the measured figures. 12 groups carry a measurement. Everything above is as the data stood on Aug 2, 2026.
